title: Dehumidifier Rental: When Renting Beats Buying (2026 Costs)
h1: Dehumidifier Rental: When Renting Beats Buying
dek: After a burst pipe, renting a restoration-grade unit can be the smart move. For a damp basement that comes back every summer, it almost never is.
description: Dehumidifier rental explained: where to rent industrial LGR units, typical daily costs, and the breakeven point where buying your own makes more sense.
intro: **Dehumidifier rental** is a real, thriving market — but only for one kind of machine. Rental counters stock commercial **LGR (low-grain refrigerant) restoration units**, the big, rugged dehumidifiers built to dry out flooded rooms. They don't rent the 30- to 50-pint units you'd put in a basement, because those cost less to buy than a few days of renting anything comparable.

That makes the rent-or-buy decision fairly simple. Rent an industrial unit for a one-time flood or burst pipe you need dried out quickly. Buy for a chronic damp basement or crawl space, or for any problem that will return next season.

The stakes are real. The Insurance Information Institute puts the average homeowners claim for water damage and freezing at more than $12,500 (based on 2017–2021 data), and the EPA notes mold can start growing on wet building materials within 24 to 48 hours. The equipment decision you make on day one matters.

blocks.text: The places that rent dehumidifiers are the same ones that rent jackhammers and floor sanders:

items: **Home Depot Tool & Truck Rental** — many locations stock LGR and some desiccant units.
**Sunbelt Rentals** and similar equipment-rental chains — broader industrial selection, including larger desiccant systems.
**Restoration-equipment rental houses** — specialists that serve water-damage contractors and often rent to homeowners too.
**Local independent rental yards** — inventory varies, but worth a call in smaller towns.

blocks.text: None of these publish one national price online. You'll get a quote by branch and rental length, with daily, weekly and four-week rates. Much of the stock is from Dri-Eaz; our [best Dri-Eaz dehumidifier](/best/best-dri-eaz-dehumidifier/) guide explains the models you're likely to see.

sections.heading: What to ask before you rent

items.label: Is it an LGR or a conventional refrigerant unit?
items.text: LGR units keep pulling water as the air dries, which shortens a dry-out. Ask for one for water-damage jobs.

items.label: What's the daily vs. weekly rate?
items.text: If you expect more than three or four days, a weekly rate is often cheaper.

items.label: Does it have a pump?
items.text: A pump lets the unit run overnight without a full bucket shutting it down. Ask for the hose too.

items.label: Will it fit in your vehicle?
items.text: Restoration units are heavy. Check dimensions, weight and whether a hand truck is included.

items.label: Do you need air movers too?
items.text: Fans that blow across wet floors and walls speed evaporation so the dehumidifier has moisture to pull. Most counters rent them alongside.

blocks.text: These are planning numbers, not quotes. Weekly and monthly rates bring the per-day cost down. Large desiccant systems used on construction and commercial jobs cost far more per day, but that tier is built for contractors rather than a homeowner's basement.

items: **One short rental (3–5 days):** usually cheaper than buying a restoration unit outright. Renting wins for a genuine one-off.
**Two rentals in a year:** you've likely spent more than an LGR unit costs to own.
**One job lasting more than 7–9 days:** rental fees can cross the purchase price on their own.
**Recurring leaks or rental property:** skip the math and buy. Our [water damage dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-water-damage/) guide covers sizing.

sections.heading: Why you can't rent a regular room dehumidifier

blocks.text: Search any rental counter and you won't find a 35- or 50-pint home unit. That's not an oversight. A standard compressor dehumidifier sells new for roughly $150 to $350 — less than a week of renting anything in a rental catalog — so there's no price at which renting one makes sense, and the industry never built that tier.

If your problem is everyday humidity, buy a residential unit sized to the space. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) and [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) picks are good places to start.

sections.heading: Getting the most from a rental unit

items: Remove standing water first with a wet vac or pump; a dehumidifier handles moisture in the air and materials, not puddles.
Pull out soaked carpet pads, baseboards and anything that can't be dried quickly.
Close the room's doors and windows so the unit only dries the affected space.
Run air movers across wet surfaces and keep the dehumidifier running continuously.
Track progress with a moisture meter or hygrometer, and return the unit once readings are back to normal.

blocks.title: Check your insurance
blocks.text: If the water damage is part of a covered claim, mitigation equipment rental is often reimbursable. Photograph the damage, keep every receipt and ask your adjuster before you start.

Rent an industrial LGR dehumidifier for a one-time flood or burst pipe you need dried within a week; home-improvement rental counters and equipment-rental chains quote them by branch. Buy once you're facing a second incident, a chronic damp space or a rental property to manage — an LGR unit like the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme pays for itself in one or two uses. For everyday humidity, skip the rental counter entirely and buy a residential unit; it's cheaper from day one.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to rent or buy a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a one-time flood, renting an LGR unit for a few days is usually cheaper than buying one. For chronic dampness, buying wins quickly — a standard residential unit costs less than two days of commercial rental.

faqs.q: Where can I rent a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Home Depot's Tool & Truck Rental, equipment-rental chains like Sunbelt Rentals, restoration-equipment rental houses and some independent rental yards. Prices are quoted by branch and rental length.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to rent an industrial dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Plan on roughly $75 to $125 a day for a restoration-grade LGR unit, less per day on weekly rates. Large industrial desiccant systems can cost hundreds of dollars a day.

faqs.q: Can you rent a small dehumidifier for a room?
faqs.a: Generally no. Rental counters stock commercial units only, because a residential dehumidifier costs less to buy than a week of renting.

faqs.q: How long should I rent a dehumidifier after a flood?
faqs.a: Most single-room dry-outs take three to five days with air movers, but larger or deeper water damage can take longer. Measure with a moisture meter rather than guessing, and consider buying if it stretches past a week.

faqs.q: Does insurance pay for dehumidifier rental?
faqs.a: Often, when the water damage is a covered loss, since drying equipment is part of mitigating further damage. Confirm with your adjuster and keep all receipts.
